behavior.hostTotalSwitch: Default OFF; CLI --p2p or host settings controls both automatic sending and P2P download entry
behavior.pageSenderPreference: Document lifetime only. One opt-out covers all subsequent PCDN events in that page; no localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie persistence. Refresh or a new document defaults ON. Host policy changes do not reset an open page's choice.
behavior.receiverIndependent: Turning sending OFF does not prevent P2P receiving or ordinary downloading
behavior.passiveSender: Capable idle pages register automatically. One passive page per active file lazily pulls, SHA-256 verifies and caches requested chunks, coalesces simultaneous same-piece pulls and shares cached chunks. No proactive full-file scan or local user file access.
behavior.passiveBounds: 512 page registrations globally, 32 per IP; one file per passive page, one origin chunk pull at a time, 90 second idle cache/task eviction. Existing file participant/cache/upload/signal budgets retained.
behavior.httpAndHttps: Both support WebRTC data transfer. Prefer WebCrypto where available; bundled ES5 SHA-256 via Worker or yielding fallback handles ordinary HTTP without WebCrypto. Native disk writes remain browser/security-context dependent.

realBrowser.environment: Two actual Chromium-based browser pages using the machine's non-loopback LAN address over ordinary HTTP; generated16MiB fixture. Same physical machine, no browser security changes.
realBrowser.idleSender: Page never selected any download; default passive role transmitted16MiB, and later reused cached content for another16MiB
realBrowser.receiver: Page sender switch OFF throughout repeated downloads; each completed with16MiB from peer and0 direct origin file bytes
realBrowser.preference: Sender OFF remained across subsequent downloads. Earlier refresh reset the page to ON as intended.

cachedTransferTraffic.interpretation: Server response-body counter delta over the cached-download observation window, including control/hash/status traffic. It is not a NIC packet capture, billing metric or production benchmark.

realBrowser.outputScope: Verified actual WebRTC reception and per-piece digest path. Final browser-save event/file was not independently captured for these ordinary-HTTP runs;2.7.0 loopback output hash verification remains separately recorded.

verification.macos: Source compatibility only; no build/test per user instruction
verification.ie11: Static syntax/capability fallback only; no new actual IE run

limits: IE and browsers without WebRTC retain ordinary downloading, not PCDN sending
Ordinary HTTP can relay arbitrary supported-size files with bounded memory; receiving without native local write APIs uses64/128MiB Blob limits, then ordinary-download fallback
Native disk streaming requires browser support and a trusted secure context; no actual save-file picker or multi-GB endurance test was performed
A passive relay's first uncached piece still comes from the host. Savings arise from reuse; the first relay-assisted transfer alone does not imply reduced host data traffic
WebRTC UDP/client isolation restrictions can force origin fallback; no external STUN/TURN added
Page choice resets on refresh/new document, and is independent across separately opened browser pages
No new third-party runtime/library dependency; Apache-2.0 project licensing retained
